subject: Data handling follow-up: field-level storage & logging retention
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@novumhealth.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo - field-level handling & logs

Hi Olivia — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap + proposed answers to the questions you raised on the call, so we have a concrete baseline for procurement/security to review. Let me know if anything needs to be adjusted.

Summary (short):
- What we store: structured metadata (request timestamp, model/version, route id), non-sensitive model telemetry, and the text of prompts/outputs only when customer enables "persist outputs".
- Field-level approach: customers can mark specific input fields as "sensitive" in the Redwood SDK; marked fields are never persisted to disk and are redacted from audit logs.
- KV/session cache: in-memory only (evicted on session end), never written to long-term storage.
- Retention windows: ephemeral debug logs are kept 30 days, structured audit logs 365 days by default (can be shortened via contract).
- Residency: hosted data can be pinned to a US region (us-east-1) for Novum. Private/Dedicated options available if you need on-prem or VPC-only.

Open items we promised to deliver:
1) SOC 2 Type II summary and brief on what evidence covers logging/retention (attached).
2) A data-handling matrix mapping "input field" -> "stored?" -> "where" -> "TTL" (attached workbook).
3) A short note from our Security PM confirming KV cache behavior and function-call argument treatment.

Concrete proposals for Novum:
- Default: keep model outputs persisted for 30 days (useful for analytics + debugging).
- If you require zero-output-persistence, we can disable persist_outputs at the account level; in that mode outputs are only held in-memory for the processing window and not written to logs.
- Sensitive-field redaction: we will provide SDK helpers to tag fields; redacted fields will be replaced with a consistent placeholder in logs ("[REDACTED]") and will not be included in exported artifacts.

Next steps:
- I'll share the attachments and loop in Aditya (security) to provide the short confirmation note by EOD tomorrow.
- Please reply with any redlines to the retention windows above or add procurement questions and I'll route them to our contracts lead.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
(415) 555-0189

From: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@novumhealth.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo - field-level handling & logs

Thanks, Lauren — this is a helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) When you say "SDK helpers to tag fields", can you confirm this works for both the HTTP API and the JS/Java SDKs? Our web UI still uses the REST endpoint for some flows.
2) For audit purposes we need a tamper-evident record of model inputs (not full text for PII). Is there a recommended approach where you store hashes of redacted inputs rather than full text?
3) What exactly falls under "non-sensitive model telemetry" vs "structured audit logs" in your wording? Examples would help.

Also, procurement asked whether the 365-day audit log window can be reduced to 180 days in the base contract, with the option to extend to 365 via SOW.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Olivia

Olivia Turner
Director, Product & Data Privacy
Novum Health
olivia.turner@novumhealth.ai
(617) 555-4420

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Quick follow-up from today's demo - field-level handling & logs

Fwding Olivia's questions to loop Security/Platform in. Draft answers below — happy to edit before we send back.

On audit hashing: we currently support storing SHA-256 digests of arbitrary strings as a tenant-scoped audit artifact; the full string can be redacted at ingestion time. That satisfies tamper-evidence plus non-reversibility if you never store the original. We should call out that salted hashes are recommendable if Novum wants deterministic but non-reversible IDs across records.

SDK tagging: field-level tags are implemented in our JS and Java SDKs and are available in the REST API via a "field_tags" JSON object on the request payload. I'll add a short code snippet to the drive link.

Telemetry vs audit logs:
- Non-sensitive telemetry: model latency percentiles, token counts (no text), error rates, model variant used.
- Structured audit logs: event-level records that include timestamps, route ids, request hashes (if configured), and flags for whether a request contained redacted fields.

Retention windows: we can offer 180d baseline for structured audit logs with an option to extend to 365d in the contract. Ephemeral debug traces (full text for debugging) are 30d unless explicitly exported.

I'll produce a one-paragraph confirmation from Security that we can send to Olivia and procurement.

- Aditya
Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@novumhealth.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Novum Health Procurement <procurement@novumhealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's demo - field-level handling & logs

Hi Olivia / procurement team — following up with the confirmed details from our Security team. Apologies for the brief delay. Answers below are what we'll include in the SOW/contract language if you proceed.

1) SDK/API field tagging: available across JS, Java, and REST ("field_tags" object). Tagging is applied at request time; tagged values are redacted prior to any persistence. SDK helpers: see code snippets in the shared Drive link.

2) Tamper-evident audit approach: we support storing SHA-256 digests (tenant-scoped) of input values at ingestion. If you prefer salted digests we can salt with a Novum-only secret (never stored on our side) to prevent cross-tenant correlation. Digests are stored as part of structured audit logs, not in debug traces.

3) Definitions: Non-sensitive telemetry = metrics (latency, token counts, model id); Structured audit logs = event records (timestamp, route id, request digest, redaction flags). Debug traces (full text) are separate and kept only when debug logging is enabled.

4) Retention windows and contractual options:
- Debug traces (full text): 30 days default; can be exported prior to purge.
- Structured audit logs: default 180 days (per procurement ask); extendable to 365 via SOW.
- Persisted outputs (model responses you choose to persist): default 30 days; account-level setting can disable persistence entirely.

5) Residency: Hosted pinning to us-east-1 available. For VPC/Private deployments we can provide on-prem or dedicated clusters in your cloud account.

Attachments included: SOC2 summary and the data handling matrix mapping fields to storage/TTL.

If these points look ok, can you confirm: (a) acceptance of 180-day audit log baseline, and (b) whether you want salted digests or plain tenant-scoped digests for audit hashing? Once you confirm we'll add the options to the MSA/SOW.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if procurement prefers to walk the items.

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
